context: Data visualization — scatterplot with marginal strip plots and box plots showing age vs. cholesterol by cardiovascular risk group, with brush-to-filter interaction updating all linked views
first_impression: A deliberately composed chart with a colorblind-safe palette, clean typographic hierarchy, and sophisticated linked-view brushing that updates marginals and a regression annotation simultaneously.
what_works: The Tol palette (#4477AA/#EE6677/#228833) is an intentional, principled choice that immediately signals design care over default categorical colors. The brush interaction linking the scatterplot to both marginal summaries and the R² regression annotation is genuinely sophisticated and well-executed.
what_doesnt: The marginal box plots collapse all three risk groups into a single aggregate distribution, losing the per-group color information the strip dots show — a missed opportunity to encode group spread in the margins. The legend is positioned overlapping the scatter data area (top-left corner of the plot), which could obscure low-risk points and feels like an afterthought placement rather than a confident design decision.
